Abstract
28
Introduction  Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-level 
29
performance in three key domains: linguistic understanding, knowledge-based 
30
reasoning, and complex problem-solving. These characteristics make LLMs valuable 
31
tools for medical education. Standardized medical examinations evaluate clinical 
32
competencies in trainees. These examinations allow rigorous verification of LLMs' 
33
accuracy and reliability in medical contexts. Current methods use standardized 
34
examinations to test LLMs' clinical reasoning abilities. Significant performance 
35
variations emerge across different clinical scenarios. No comprehensive reviews have 
36
compared different LLM versions in medical examinations. Most studies focus on 
37
individual models, lacking comparative analyses of multiple LLM versions. Current 
38
approaches struggle to keep pace with evolving research needs. This study synthesizes 
39
extant research on LLMs in medical examinations , by analyzing the current 
40
challenges and limitations, offers guidance for future investigations.
41
Methods and analysis  The protocol was designed following the JBI 
42
Manual for Evidence Synthesis guidelines. We established explicit 
43
inclusion/exclusion criteria and search strategies. Systematic searches were performed 
44
in PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection databases. The methodology details 
45
literature screening, data extraction, analysis frameworks, and process mapping. This 
46
approach ensures methodological rigor throughout the research process.
47
Ethics and dissemination  This protocol outlines a scoping review 
48
methodology. The study involves systematic synthesis and analysis of published

Strengths and limitations of this study
52
(1)This scoping review programme strictly adheres to the standardized guidelines 
53
for the implementation of scoping reviews. Includes the JBI Manual for Evidence 
54
Synthesis and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Scoping 
55
Reviews Extended Meta-Analysis (PRISMA- ScR) guideline.
56
(2)The search strategy included two databases:PubMed, Web of Science Core 
57
Collection.
58
(3)This scoping review will bridge the knowledge gap of LLMs across medical 
59
examinations due to recent rapid technological advances.
60
(4)By the nature of the scoping review, failure to critically evaluate identified 
61
sources of evidence.
62
The results of the scoping review will serve as a basis for identifying directions for 
63
further research on LLMs in the field of medical examinations.
64
Introduction
65
Recently, the swift advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, 
66
notably Large Language Models (LLMs), has ushered in fresh prospects for medical 
67
education and examination. These models, trained with deep learning architectures and 
68
large-scale corpora, are able to generate, understand, and process natural language texts, 
69
and have demonstrated near-human level capabilities in language comprehension and 
70
intellectual reasoning. LLMs have emerged as powerful tools across diverse

71
educational domains, particularly in professional fields such as medicine, law, and 
72
business[1], where they facilitate both specialized knowledge acquisition and statistical 
73
software training[2]. Their application in medical education has shown especially 
74
promising potential.
75
Medical examinations play a crucial role in the medical education pathway, can 
76
assess  the readiness of medical students for clinical practice. In recent years, 
77
researchers have increasingly utilized standardised tests, such as medical licensing 
78
exams in various languages and countries/regions, to evaluate the performance of 
79
LLMs and their ability to apply medical knowledge. The ability of LLMs to provide 
80
answers to complex queries [1] has made their potential as an educational tool in the 
81
field of medical examinations increasingly apparent. 
82
For example, OpenAI's ChatGPT powered by the GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 models[3], 
83
has achieved significant results in several examinations, including the Neurosurgery 
84
Written Board Examinations[4], the UK Radiology Fellowship Examinations[5], and the 
85
Dental Licensing Examinations[6]. Both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 exceeded passing 
86
thresholds, with GPT-4 achieving particularly notable results. The GPT-4 model further 
87
strengthened in the proportion of facts and questions answered correctly with logically 
88
consistent reasoning, demonstrating near-human level performance on a variety of 
89
professional and academic benchmarks[7].
90
Similarly, Google Bard (now Gemini), developed by Google, utilizes the Pathways 
91
Language Model (PaLM)2 architecture[3]. Gemini has exceeded passing thresholds in 
92
multiple standardized examinations, including the Family Medicine In-Training

Exam[8], the Ophthalmology Knowledge Assessment[9], and the Japanese national 
94
dental hygienist examination[10].
95
Similarly,Microsoft Copilot (formerly Bing Chat) utilizes the GPT-4 architecture, 
96
It has demonstrated proficiency in medical examinations, including the Korean 
97
Emergency Medicine Board Examination[11] and the Peruvian National Licensing 
98
Medical Examination[12].  LLM success extends beyond English-language medical 
99
examinations. These models have proven effective across multiple languages, countries, 
100
and medical specialties. This is evidenced by performance in the Spanish Medical 
101
Residency Entrance Examination (MIR)[13] and the Intercollegiate Membership of the 
102
Royal College of Surgeons examination[14]. 
103
Studies indicate that although LLMs exhibit strong overall performance, they may 
104
fall short of meeting performance benchmarks in specialized domains. In the Japanese 
105
Society of Radiology Official Board Exam[15]. ChatGPT achieved 40.8% accuracy, 
106
GPT-4 reached 65%, and Google Bard scored 38.8%. For the American Board of 
107
Anesthesiology (ABA) Examination[16], only GPT-4 attained passing scores. It 
108
achieved 78% accuracy in basic components and 80% in advanced sections. GPT-3 
109
scored 58% (basic) and 50% (advanced), while Google Bard achieved 47% and 46% 
110
respectively.
111
LLMs demonstrate exceptional performance in handling fill-in-the-blank, short-
112
answer queries, and expository questions[17]. The ability to accurately answer multiple 
113
questions based on an article or chart is evident. However, the performance was less 
114
effective in handling tasks involving analog data, providing detailed written

116
regulations, policies, and languages create training gaps, leading to superior 
117
performance in English-language contexts.
118
While existing studies have preliminarily validated the potential of LLMs in 
119
medical examinations, their capacity to comprehensively evaluate multilingual, 
120
multidisciplinary, and multi-format examinations remains largely unexplored. In 
121
addition, the majority of existing research has primarily focused on the performance of 
122
the models. There is relatively limited discussion regarding the analysis of the causes 
123
of their errors and potential directions for improvement. Therefore, this study aims to 
124
construct a comprehensive framework for measuring medical examinations. It 
125
evaluates LLMs performance across clinical scenarios. The research explores LLMs 
126
applications in medical education and further promote the innovation and development 
127
of AI technology in the medical field. Scoping review through this program, answer the 
128
following research questions, see Table 1. The purpose of this scoping review program 
129
is to address the aforementioned questions, provide an overview of recent developments, 
130
and identify major trends. It also aims to guide future research by highlighting the open 
131
challenges and limitations of current methods. 
132

Methods and analysis
135
A scoping review serves as a systematic synthesis of existing knowledge[18]. This 
136
methodology aims to address exploratory research questions through comprehensive 
137
searching, screening, and evaluation of published literature. It identifies key concepts, 
138
evidence categories, and research gaps within specific domains. The scoping review 
139
will adhere to the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis, chapter 11: Scoping reviews. 
140
Compliance with the specifications of the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic 
141
Reviews and Meta-Meta Analyses Extended for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA)[19]. The 
142
study outlines specific methodological components with detailed specifications. It 
143
covers the entire process of inclusion and exclusion criteria, literature search strategy, 
144
sources of evidence, data extraction, analysis of the evidence, and final presentation of 
145
the results. These aspects will be elaborated upon in the subsequent chapters.
146

3.

The search query we employed encompassed two databases: PubMed and the Web 
163
of Science Core Collection. Initially, the search queries were primarily focused on 
164
PubMed and were subsequently adapted to ensure compatibility with the other database. 
165
The aim was to automate the process as much as possible. The literature search for this 
166
study was restricted to scholarly publications dated from January 1, 2020, to the 
167
present.The delineation of this time window is based on the following two 
168
considerations:First, by concentrating on literature published within the past five years, 
169
we can effectively capture the cutting-edge developments in the discipline while

171
Second, considering that the medical AI field is characterized by a short cycle of 
172
technology updates. The five-year framework strikes a balance between the 
173
comprehensiveness of knowledge updates and the feasibility of systematic reviews, 
174
ensuring the incorporation of the most recent evidence while maintaining the clarity 
175
and operability of research boundaries. The details of each search string - including the 
176
number of retrieved records, date range, and search date will be documented using the 
177
standardized template established by the Karolinska Institute[20].
178
Following the study selection process, a forward search (SOE) will be conducted 
179
on the reference lists of included articles to ensure comprehensive coverage.This 
180
procedure aims to identify potentially relevant studies overlooked during the 
181
preliminary search. Systematic examination of references from selected studies will 
182
identify theme-related literature and expand the research scope. 
183
Source of evidence
184
Evidence source selection defines appropriate literature types and data sources for 
185
inclusion. The finalized search strategy will be implemented across both databases. 
186
Following search completion, results were deduplicated to eliminate redundant 
187
entries.  An initial screening phase was conducted on retrieved records. This 
188
screening involved title/abstract evaluation against predefined inclusion/exclusion 
189
criteria. Studies satisfying all inclusion criteria during initial screening were retained 
190
for full-text review. Studies passing initial screening underwent full-text appraisal. 
191

Analysis of evidence and presentation of results
205
Descriptive analysis was employed to systematically categorize the compiled 
206
evidence. This methodological approach aims to establish a comprehensive overview 
207
of current research status. Graphical data visualization techniques were implemented to 
208
evaluate LLMs accuracy in medical examination contexts. Percentage as the main 
209
quantitative indicator. This presentation not only visualizes the difference in 
210
performance between different LLMs across examination. It also provides a data base 
211
for exploring the sub-questions in the study (see Table 1 for details). Annotated 
212
graphical elements with explanatory captions ensure precise data interpretation. These 
213
annotations provide contextual framework, data significance clarification, and 
214
standardized interpretation guidelines.

key_findings.claim: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 exceeded passing thresholds in multiple medical licensing examinations including the Neurosurgery Written Board Examinations, UK Radiology Fellowship Examinations, and Dental Licensing Examinations, with GPT-4 achieving particularly notable results
key_findings.context: Reported as background evidence motivating the scoping review; sourced from cited primary studies

key_findings.claim: GPT-4 achieved 65% accuracy on the Japanese Society of Radiology Official Board Exam, outperforming ChatGPT (40.8%) and Google Bard (38.8%)
key_findings.context: Illustrates that LLMs may fall short in specialized domains even when overall performance is strong

key_findings.claim: Only GPT-4 attained passing scores on the American Board of Anesthesiology (ABA) Examination, with GPT-3 and Google Bard both failing to reach passing thresholds
key_findings.quantitative_result: GPT-4: 78% basic / 80% advanced; GPT-3: 58% basic / 50% advanced; Bard: 47% basic / 46% advanced
key_findings.context: Demonstrates substantial inter-model performance variation in high-stakes specialized medical examinations

key_findings.claim: LLMs perform better on fill-in-the-blank, short-answer, and expository questions than on tasks involving analog data, detailed written explanations, or complex queries
key_findings.context: Question format is an important moderator of LLM performance in medical examinations

key_findings.claim: LLMs demonstrate superior performance in English-language medical examinations compared to non-English contexts due to training data distribution biases and gaps in national healthcare regulation coverage
key_findings.context: Identified as a key challenge for deploying LLMs globally across multilingual medical education systems

key_findings.claim: Google Bard/Gemini (PaLM2 architecture) exceeded passing thresholds in multiple standardized examinations including the Family Medicine In-Training Exam, Ophthalmology Knowledge Assessment, and Japanese national dental hygienist examination
key_findings.context: Demonstrates cross-model and cross-language generalizability of LLM performance in medical examinations

key_findings.claim: No comprehensive reviews have systematically compared different LLM versions across multilingual, multidisciplinary, and multi-format medical examinations; existing literature primarily focuses on individual models without comparative analysis
key_findings.context: Core knowledge gap justifying the proposed scoping review

key_findings.claim: Existing research on LLMs in medical examinations provides limited analysis of error causes and improvement directions, focusing predominantly on performance metrics
key_findings.context: Identified gap addressed by research sub-question RQ.06 on error type classification

llm_extraction.methods_summary: Scoping review protocol designed following JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis (Chapter 11) and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Systematic searches conducted in two databases: PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection. Literature restricted to January 1, 2020 to present. A three-step search strategy was employed: preliminary searches to identify key terms, iterative refinement of search queries, and forward citation searching from included articles. Two-stage screening process: title/abstract evaluation followed by full-text review against predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria. Data extraction using structured charting tables capturing publication details, model characteristics (category, application, accuracy), and examination type/question format. Descriptive analysis using accuracy percentage as primary quantitative indicator with graphical visualization. Search documentation follows standardized Karolinska Institute template.
llm_extraction.limitations: Scoping review methodology does not include critical quality appraisal of individual evidence sources, limiting ability to weight findings by study rigor. Search restricted to only two databases (PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection), potentially missing relevant literature indexed in other repositories (e.g., Embase, Scopus, IEEE Xplore). This is a protocol paper describing planned methods; no empirical synthesis has been conducted. The planned review covers only published literature from 2020 onward, potentially excluding earlier foundational work. No meta-analytic pooling of effect sizes is planned due to scoping review design. Language restrictions are not explicitly stated in the protocol.

methodology_details.approach: Scoping review protocol following JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis and PRISMA-ScR with structured database searching, two-stage screening, and standardized data extraction charting
methodology_details.reproducibility_notes: Search strategy to be documented using Karolinska Institute standardized template recording retrieved record counts, date ranges, and search dates. Protocol pre-registered with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and data extraction template (Box 1). Any protocol amendments will be documented with date and rationale.
